title: Rangers Aud renovation and new restaurant, parks plan
subtitle: Also covered: Parks Master Plan, tree and bench dedication changes, noise exemptions and licensing penalty by-law amendments.
overview: The committee recommended that the Kitchener Rangers renovate the players' dressing room area, business office and media/scouts room at The Aud, and that the City build a new restaurant there at the same time, with $2,000,000 in funding {{vote:m4}}. The Rangers lead the work and pay for their portion. Staff said the restaurant cost would be repaid to the tax base over several years. Construction is planned for the off-season.

The committee also recommended approving the Places Parks Master Plan, which sets a 10-year direction for park quality and includes near-, mid- and long-term priorities {{vote:m5}}. It recommended a revised Park Tree and Bench Dedication Program {{vote:m6}}. Under it, the City owns benches and trees, and donors hold a plaque for a fixed term.

On consent, the committee recommended noise exemptions for Downtown Special Events {{vote:m1}} and the Greek Food Festival on June 7 and 8 {{vote:m2}}. It also recommended by-law changes to move Licensing violations into the Administrative Monetary Penalty System {{vote:m3}}. Council must still adopt these recommendations.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the Rangers' requested renovations, with the Rangers leading the project, and $2,000,000 for a City-built restaurant at The Aud.
The committee recommended approving the Parks Master Plan - Places and directing staff to carry out its near-, mid- and long-term implementation framework.

decisions.item: Park Tree and Bench Dedication Program
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the revised program, which replaces the informal process and the fixed 2015 pricing.
The committee recommended a by-law amending By-law 2024-01 and Chapters 553 and 599 to move Licensing enforcement and adjudication into the Administrative Monetary Penalty System.
The committee recommended an exemption to Chapter 450 (Noise) for all Downtown Special Events as outlined in the staff report.
The committee recommended a noise exemption for the festival at 527 Bridgeport Road on June 7 (12pm-11pm) and June 8 (12pm-10pm), 2025.

debate: On the Aud, the Rangers' chief operating officer said competition for players has grown, citing other Ontario Hockey League clubs' renovations and players' option to play US college hockey. Councillors asked whether the plan went far enough. The Rangers said it would serve for a decade or more.

Councillors asked about funding for the restaurant. Staff said $575,000 comes from the capital contingency account, with the rest from the Aud ticket reserve and the Municipal Accommodation Tax. Staff said the restaurant revenue would repay the tax base. One councillor asked whether the region should help fund the facility.

Questions on the Aud's future and restaurant: staff said a venue assessment and strategic roadmap will begin in 2026 and go to the next term of Council. They said the new restaurant would be separate from the existing one and open regular hours, with local food and drink being considered.

On the Parks Master Plan, one councillor worried about infrastructure costs from washrooms, drinking water and lighting. Staff said washroom and water strategies would return to Council first, and lighting criteria would avoid unnecessary lighting. Another councillor wanted downtown sites such as the Bramm Yards to have real green space, not paved areas. Staff said that site's own master plan would guide it.

On tree and bench dedications, councillors asked about plaque theft and how donations would work. Staff said bench plaques are harder to remove, and a $50 donation goes to a memorial forest with several locations, not a single chosen tree.
